coverage.note: Thorough overview spanning demand projections, grid constraints, capacity pricing, supply/vacancy, hyperscaler capex, and gas-vs-renewable shift; all major dimensions present.

sourcing.note: Claims attributed to varied, plausible sources (IEA/Pew, LBNL/DOE, GS, S&P/451, Grid Strategies, EIA, CBRE, IEEFA, Deloitte, GEM); quantitative figures consistently cited.

data_integrity.note: Comps multiples are internally consistent and plausible (NRG 136x and GEV 70x flagged as trough), though some EV/EPS figures hard to verify and CLNE is a stub.

analytical_quality.note: Five differentiated theses with peer-relative valuation logic, explicit risks, sizing guidance, and a clear exclusion rationale for omitted names.

actionability.note: Priority stack with specific next steps per name (model PJM curves, PPA tracking, margin timeline, rate cases) makes it directly usable by a junior analyst.

Claude.summary: Institutional-quality primer with strong sourcing, comprehensive coverage, and sharp differentiated idea generation; only minor data-verification gaps in the comps table hold back data integrity.

coverage.note: Broadly covers demand growth, supply constraints, pricing, geography, utility/grid impacts and some policy context, but skimps on market structure/economics by value chain and omits a fuller regulatory treatment.

sourcing.note: Most overview claims are attributed to named sources and are reasonably varied, but several thesis-critical assertions in the Ideas are unsourced or second-hand and some sources are advocacy/media rather than primary data.

data_integrity.note: Comps contain red flags: GEV EV/EBITDA looks implausibly inflated without reconciliation, NRG/ETR/AES valuation inputs may be stale or mismatched, and the table lacks dates/NTM-LTM basis needed to validate the numbers.

analytical_quality.note: Ideas are clearly written and differentiated, but several theses overstate certainty, rely on loose valuation analogies, and use peer/multiple logic that is not always apples-to-apples across merchant, regulated, and equipment names.

actionability.note: A junior analyst could use this as a solid starting point given the priority stack and suggested workstreams, though it still needs source verification, cleaner comps, and explicit model assumptions before real investment use.

GPT.summary: Good thematic primer with strong narrative framing and useful next steps, but it falls short of institutional quality because the comps need tighter validation, sourcing in the stock theses is inconsistent, and the valuation framework mixes very different business models too loosely.
